section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains how the aspect of Mah in holiness gives rise to the aspect of Mah in the other side, through the klipah of Re’umah, and how sins cause the life-force of holiness to be spilled into the domain of evil.
section.t: And the explanation of the matter:
Behold,
just as there is an aspect of Mah in holiness, so too there is an aspect of Mah in the other side,
and this is the matter of “and his concubine, and her name was Re’umah,”
“Re’u Mah” (see what).
And the matter in this:
Behold,
the possibility for matters of the other side is because they have a place given to them in holiness,
and as we see in the service of the soul,
that when one serves his service in self-nullification,
but in a manner that he feels the self-nullification,
behold this is a giving of place that from this will come an aspect of yeshus (selfhood),
and this is,
that initially the self-nullification will be in a manner of yeshus,
this is the matter of the klipah of Re’umah,
“Re’u Mah,”
and afterward it will come to complete yeshus,
which is absolute evil.
And so too it is in the chain of descent of the worlds,
that through the klipah of Re’u Mah, which is opposite the world of Atzilus,
behold, in the multiplicity of descent, absolute evil branches forth from it,
the aspect of Mah of the other side.
And concerning this it is said,
“He who sheds
the blood of man within man,”
for “man” (Adam) in gematria is Mah,
behold, through sins he sheds the blood of the man of holiness,
the aspect of Mah of holiness,
into the man of Belial,
which is the aspect of Mah of the other side.
And the matter in this:
Behold,
the 248 positive commandments and 365 negative commandments correspond to the 248 limbs and 365 sinews,
for the matter of the limbs is that they draw down the life-force,
and they limit the life-force so that it will not be drawn outward,
and when one cuts the limb, then the life-force is drawn outward,
and likewise regarding the sinews, through which is the flow of blood,
and so too when one transgresses a positive or negative commandment, he causes the life-force and blood of holiness to be drawn outward.
And this is what is said,
“And he who pierces the Name of Havayah,”
for behold, all the commandments are dependent on the Name Havayah,
and when one sinned and blemished and diverted the path, by this that he transgresses one of the commandments of Havayah,
behold he pierces the Name of Havayah,
and through this he sheds the blood of the man of holiness into the man of Belial.
And this is also what our sages, of blessed memory, said,
“Titus cut the Curtain and blood came out of it,”
and this is,
that they showed him how it is possible for the matter of the destruction to be,
that it is not in his own power,
but only through the blemish that was made by this that they spilled the blood,
the innerness of the life-force,
of the man of holiness,
into the man of Belial.
And based on this, there is yet another interpretation of what is said, “Remember, Havayah, what (Mah) has been to us,”
that our Mah has become the Mah of the other side.
And this matter is accomplished through the first interpretation of “what has been to us,”
that the aspect of Mah of holiness is in concealment and hiding,
and from this it descends further downward,
so that the aspect of Mah of holiness becomes the aspect of Mah of the other side,
in the manner of the matter of “he who sheds the blood of man within man.”

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the concept of the “widowhood” of the Congregation of Israel in exile, the lack of union between Zeir Anpin and Malchus, and the prayer that God’s encompassing light should see and act upon their disgrace.
section.t: And the verse continues, “Look and see our disgrace.”
And the matter in this:
Behold, it is written,
“The disgrace of your widowhood you shall no longer remember,”
for in the time of exile the Congregation of Israel is called a widow,
as it is said,
“She has become like a widow,”
and our sages, of blessed memory, said,
“Like a widow, but not a literal widow,
like a woman whose husband has gone to a country overseas.”
Behold,
the woman is the Congregation of Israel and her husband is the Holy One, blessed be He,
and “a woman whose husband has gone to a country overseas” means that the union of the Congregation of Israel with the Holy One, blessed be He, is lacking,
and in the matter of the Sefiros it is the union of Zeir Anpin and Nukvah,
for the woman is the aspect of Malchus,
and her husband is the aspect of Zeir Anpin,
and “a woman whose husband has gone to a country overseas” means,
that the aspect of Zeir Anpin
(is not drawn down to Malchus,
but rather)
has departed to the aspect of the sea of Chochmah,
and this is that in the time of exile, Kudsha Brich Hu ascends higher and higher,
Kudsha Brich Hu is the aspect of Zeir Anpin,
and in the time of exile He ascends higher and higher,
higher to the aspect of Binah and higher to the aspect of Chochmah.
And this is the matter of “widow” (almanah),
as it is stated in the Pardes,
that “almanah” is “El manah,”
“manah” is one hundred zuz,
twice fifty,
and this is the fifty gates of Binah, as they are from below upward and from above downward,
through which is accomplished the elevation of the emotions and the drawing down of Ein Sof in the aspect of the emotions,
so that through this it will be drawn down below in the aspect of Malchus.
And this is also the matter of the journeys,
“their goings forth according to their journeys… their journeys according to their goings forth,”
which is the matter of elevation and drawing down.
But in the time of exile it is “El manah,”
that the matter of the elevation and drawing down through the fifty gates is lacking,
and therefore it is not drawn from the aspect of Zeir Anpin to Malchus to be the union of Zeir Anpin and Nukvah,
and this is the matter of “widow” (almanah).
And there is another interpretation of “almanah,”
as stated in Sefer HaShorashim,
that “almanah” is from the word “ileim” (mute).
Behold,
according to the interpretation that “almanah” is from “El manah,”
that her ketubah is a manah,
it is not understood why a male is also called “alman,”
and it must be said that because a woman is called “almanah,”
therefore a male is also called “alman.”
But according to the interpretation that “almanah” is from the word “ileim,”
it works out well that a male is also called “alman,”
because the joy of the union of the husband with his wife is lacking.
And the matter in this:
For when the revelation of the voice shines in speech, then the speech shines in revelation,
and when the speech shines in revelation, then “He will subdue peoples under us”
(for through “y’daber” from the word for speech, it also becomes “y’daber” from the word for governance),
that Israel are in the supreme level, etc.,
but when the voice is not in revelation, then the speech is in concealment in exile,
and this is the matter of “almanah” from the word “ileim.”
And concerning this we ask, “Look and see our disgrace,”
for even though “looking” (habatah) is an aspect of makif (encompassing light),
nevertheless,
behold it is effective also in the innerness,
as it is said,
“For Havayah your God walks in the midst of your camp to deliver you…,”
“to deliver you” means to be a shadow over your head,
which is an aspect of makif,
and nevertheless through this is accomplished “to deliver you” in its simple sense,
from the word for rescue,
and particularly regarding the effect on the klipot,
behold, the encompassing light blinds the eyes of the external forces
(as above).

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section concludes that when the service of “walking humbly” is lacking, the Mah of holiness becomes the Mah of the other side, and we ask God to remember and look upon our disgrace until the disgrace of widowhood is no more.
section.t: And this is what is said, “Remember, Havayah, what (Mah) has been to us…,”
Behold,
the Holy One, blessed be He, demands of Israel, “Remember your Creator in the days of your youth,”
as long as the Holy Temple stands, which is called the House of Choice,
as long as the covenant of the priesthood stands,
and as long as the covenant of the Levites stands,
and the demand is to do justice, love kindness, and walk humbly with your God,
but when the service of “walking humbly” is lacking,
which is the opposite of the matter of “Re’u Mah,”
then the Mah of the other side is made.
And for this we ask, “Remember, Havayah, what has been to us,”
that the Mah of holiness is in concealment and hiding,
and even to the point that through this the Mah of the other side is made,
and therefore, “Look and see our disgrace,”
until “the disgrace of your widowhood you shall no longer remember.”
